title: Escobar: Fort Bliss data center to shrink, shift site and use brackish water
source_used: KFOX (pool link, fetched text; the full statement from the page's structured data)
key_facts: On Monday 5 Oct 2026 US Rep. Veronica Escobar released a statement on 'positive developments' for the planned Fort Bliss data center, after the Army and the Carlyle Group held a meeting of El Paso community stakeholders.
She said the location has been moved but is still too close to residential areas, and she will keep pushing for a different location.
She said water use will likely be brackish water sent to the Kay Bailey Hutchison plant for desalination, which she called a positive development.

The scale of the data center has been reduced, but it is still on track to use gas generation, which she called an additional serious concern for air quality; she will keep pushing for renewable energy.
She had asked that the data center be moved far from any neighborhood, preserve water, use renewable energy and be transparent and accountable.
Escobar says her team first learned of the project in March.
quote_evidence: Today we learned that the location of the data center has indeed been moved, but it is still too close to residential areas.
We also learned that their water use will likely be of brackish water that will be sent to the Kay Bailey Hutchison Plant for desalination, which I see as a positive development.
The gas generation for power remains an additional serious concern.
why_it_matters_hint: A planned data center on an Army base next to El Paso is changing in response to local concern, but its congresswoman says the site, the air-quality risk from gas power and the water plan are not settled.
notes: The account is the congresswoman's statement about what the Army and Carlyle told stakeholders; neither is quoted. The statement's details (size, new site) are not given.
